tabs.title: Company Overview
tabs.content:
**Foxglove Interactive** is a game studio that operates a cross-platform multiplayer title with seasonal tournaments. The back end is a set of Python services.

**Current Environment:**
- Match telemetry and player data are stored in **Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL**. A container named `match-events` currently uses `/gameMode` as its partition key; there are only five game modes.
- Player inventories (owned items, currency) live in a container named `inventories` partitioned by `/playerId`. Several game services update the same inventory document concurrently.
- An in-game support assistant suggests fixes by finding previously **resolved support tickets** that are semantically similar to a player's new ticket. Ticket text embeddings (1536 dimensions) are produced by an embedding model.
- **Azure Managed Redis** is already deployed for session caching.

tabs.title: Requirements
tabs.content:
**Telemetry Requirements:**
- During tournaments, writes to `match-events` are throttled with 429 errors even though total provisioned throughput is far above the workload. The dominant read pattern retrieves all events for one match.

**Inventory Requirements:**
- When two services update the same inventory document at nearly the same time, neither update may silently overwrite the other; the losing writer must detect the conflict and retry against the latest state.

**Support Assistant Requirements:**
- Similar-ticket lookup must run against the embeddings stored in Azure Managed Redis and return the top 5 most similar resolved tickets by cosine similarity in single-digit milliseconds.
- All services authenticate with managed identities; no keys in source code.
